target: branch (PO_0025073) with position lateral (sensu botany) (FLOPO_0991380), pattern 18; in an inflorescence context second order inflorescence axis (PO_0006321)
reason: Eugenia, Heckeldora and Polyscias use it for the lateral axes of the inflorescence. PO already has 'secondary axis' as a synonym of branch. Adding 'axis' to the bearer list of the 'lateral' context word resolves it. Narrower than branch.

target: nectary (PO_0009035), apex region (region pattern, as for other organ apices)
reason: The apex of the nectary scales of Rhodiola/Pseudosedum and of the tepal nectary of Wurmbea. Emarginate, dentate and entire are edge or apex qualities of that region.

Only in Bulbophyllum descriptions (Bosser, in French). It is not a standard term in PO or in the orchid glossaries; it may be a garbled 'stelidium' (a column tooth) but this cannot be confirmed without the source.

target: inflorescence (PO_0009049), count of its 3-flowered partial inflorescences (pattern 03, part within a whole)
reason: '5–9 triplets of flowers' (Psoralea, Calceolaria) counts flower groups of three in an inflorescence. A group of three flowers is a count pattern, not a new structure.

In Combretum it means the primary radial walls of the peltate scales (a count of the scale's cells), but in mosses 'primary walls' are walls of the exostome teeth. It is a homonym, and PO has no cell-wall class for the scale count. Do not ground it without the parent word.

Exact: PO lists 'first order inflorescence branch' as a synonym of PO_0006321. All the examples (Medusanthera, Cryosophila) are inflorescence branches. PO_0020122 also carries the same synonym, which is worth reporting upstream.

It means different things in different groups: the apothecial margin of a lichen (Ocellularia, outside PO), a flap round the staminal ring (Eschweilera) and a fern indusium flap.

Narrower: a small raceme within a compound inflorescence (Polyscias). The Attalea example is a mistranslation of 'ráquila' (rachilla), which should go to the rachilla rule instead.

reason: A groove is a surface feature of the leaf (Sagina) or the achene (Alisma), not a separate part. Express it as grooved plus the abaxial surface.
Narrower: extra minute areolar spines of Opuntia. Cactus spines are spine leaves; 'additional very small' is a modifier.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) at the apex of its whole (pattern 18 / region apex)
reason: Dirca: a count of hairs at the apex of an organ. Trichome is the bearer and 'apical' gives its position.
Narrower: in Ericameria and Heterotheca, the axillary fascicles are leaf clusters borne on axillary short shoots. Present/absent is pattern 15.
Bearer plus position. Axillary is an existing FLOPO value whose bearers include PO:0009049.
Exact in context: in ferns (Thelypteris, Schizaea) it is the lamina tissue between the veins. 'tissue laminar expanded' is a fragment saying the lamina is expanded.

A fragment of 'fewer than 10 leaves clustered at apex' (Carex): an arrangement and a count of leaves, not a part.
A typo for 'body' in Juncus seed descriptions ('seed body clear to yellow-brown'). If fixed, the bearer is the seed (PO_0009010).
Narrower: in Ericameria, 1–2 collateral nerves run beside the midrib, which makes them lateral veins.
